audit_findings.title: Parent numerator may contain consolidated San Mateo add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; exposure scales include $28.1 million, computed as Five Point's 49% share of 2025 midstream D&A of $57.4 million, and $118.4 million of 2025 midstream capital expenditures attributable to non-controlling interests
audit_findings.mechanism: A parent-attributable OE numerator must add back noncash charges and deduct maintenance capital on the same 51% San Mateo ownership basis; inconsistent allocation directly changes anchor OE and every scenario PV.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company and Five Point own 51% and 49% of San Mateo, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved perimeter possibility, not a demonstrated error, because the supplied record does not show the ownership allocation of each OE component. It is nevertheless reasonably capable of changing the conclusion: the identified San Mateo allocation scales are substantial relative to the $717.7 million anchor and the $353.0 million equity-value gap between the $59.15 market price and $56.34 buy-below threshold. Full consolidated add-backs would overstate value, while deduction of excessive consolidated capital could understate it.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 OE line by line, identify every San Mateo amount, allocate San Mateo income, D&A, accretion, working-capital effects and maintenance capital consistently at 51%, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below calculation.

audit_findings.title: Rapid shale declines make maintenance capital the critical unsupported assumption
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 D/C/E cash capital expenditures were $1,542.3 million versus $717.7 million of anchor OE, while production increased 21%
audit_findings.mechanism: Maintenance capital is deducted in OE; understating the drilling and completion spending required to offset well declines inflates anchor OE, projected growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: By their nature, our oil and natural gas wells will experience rapid initial production declines.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates rapid initial well declines, but it does not demonstrate that the valuation's maintenance-capital deduction is sufficient. The error amount remains unresolved because 2025 capital supported 21% production growth and cannot simply be treated as maintenance. The issue is material because annual D/C/E spending exceeded twice the OE anchor and roughly half of scenario value comes from terminal value, where an overstated sustainable OE base is perpetuated.
audit_findings.action: Separate 2025 D/C/E and midstream spending into replacement and expansion capital using parent-attributable decline curves, beginning and ending production capacity, reserve conversions and well-level replacement economics; rerun the DCF using capital sufficient to hold production and required midstream capacity flat.

audit_findings.title: Future minimum-volume charges may be absent from the 2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $3,064.0 million of filed remaining obligations at December 31, 2025, including $201.4 million due within one year; the incremental net burden is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future external fees or deficiency payments reduce OE and potentially alter sustainable growth; San Mateo intercompany fees require consolidation and 49% non-controlling-interest treatment, while improved takeaway or pricing can offset the cost.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our long-term contractual obligations under agreements with minimum volume commitments totaled approximately $3.06 billion over the terms of the agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations are demonstrated, but omission from the valuation is only an unresolved possibility. Their scale is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion: the first-year scheduled amount equals 28.1% of the $717.7 million anchor, and the total is 30.3% of base equity value. Those gross figures are not a valuation deduction because services and pricing benefits are received, and San Mateo amounts are partly intercompany. Direction is therefore mixed until the net external and non-controlling-interest leakage is established.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual contract schedule by counterparty, start date, committed volume and deficiency formula; eliminate consolidated intercompany amounts, retain Five Point's economic share where applicable, quantify transportation and pricing benefits, and rerun each scenario with the resulting net cash costs.

audit_findings.title: Abandonment cash obligations may exceed the expense retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $150.4 million filed ARO at December 31, 2025, including $135.6 million due after five years; 2025 accretion was $7.8 million and settlements were $1.7 million; proved-reserve future abandonment costs were $236.2 million
audit_findings.mechanism: OE should bear the parent-attributable cash cost of plugging, removal and remediation exactly once; using accretion alone may misstate recurring cash needs, while a separate bridge deduction would double count costs already included in maintenance capital or OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s asset retirement obligations primarily relate to future costs associated with plugging and abandonment of its oil, natural gas and salt water disposal wells, removal of pipelines, equipment and facilities from leased acreage and returning such land to its original condition.
audit_findings.explanation: No demonstrated error is established because the record does not show whether maintenance capital or the OE forecast already captures abandonment cash flows. The filed $150.4 million obligation equals about $1.20 per diluted share and 2.0% of bear equity value, while the $236.2 million reserve estimate equals about $1.88 per share and 3.1% of bear equity value. These scales are potentially relevant near the $59.15 market price and $61.01 bear value, but they do not establish the incremental, correctly timed valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the undiscounted parent-attributable settlement schedule by asset, reconcile it to the reserve forecast's $236.2 million abandonment costs and the $150.4 million ARO, identify amounts already included in maintenance capital, and rerun only for the incremental cash burden not otherwise captured.
